Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the government is building a modern sports ecosystem through school and grassroots programmes, Khelo India Centres and Olympic-standard training under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).

 

Felicitating India’s Asian Para Games 2026 contingent for its record haul of 114 medals, the Prime Minister urged the athletes to build on their success as they prepare for the Los Angeles 2028 Games.

 

The Prime Minister also recalled his appeal from the Red Fort encouraging young people to participate in a nationwide talent hunt with the Olympics in focus.

 

Interacting with the contingent at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi, PM Modi said the performance reflected India’s emergence as a major global sporting power. He congratulated the athletes, their families, coaches and trainers, saying the players had won both medals and the hearts of millions.

India secured 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, alongside five world records and nine Asian records.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the Martyrs’ Memorial of the First War of Independence of 1857 in Haryana’s Ambala, saying it will inspire patriotism among younger generations and honour the sacrifices of India’s freedom fighters. Built at a cost of 594 crore rupees across 22 acres, the memorial features 22 galleries combining historical documents, traditional craftsmanship and digital technology. Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and Union Minister Manohar Lal were among those present.

Addressing the gathering, Mr Shah said revolutionary fighters had launched an armed struggle against British rule in Ambala Cantonment on May 10, 1857, and that the movement subsequently spread across the country, shaking the foundations of the British Empire.

 

He criticised historians who described the events of 1857 as a revolt, invoking Veer Savarkar’s description of the struggle as a war for freedom.

The Indian Coast Guard has launched a massive hunt to locate the fishermen that went missing during cyclone Murasu. While bodies of three fishermen from Tamil Nadu washed ashore at Kothapatnam coast in Ongole in Andhra Pradesh were found, another fisherman’s body was found later in the sea by the Coast Guard.

 

The search is underway for the remaining 5 fishermen. Three boats set out from Tamil Nadu for fishing on October 29. Due to the impact of Cyclone Murasu, two boats were anchored for safety near Ramayapatnam Port on Monday, while the third boat proceeded towards Nizampatnam Port. The nine fishermen on the third boat departed from Nizampatnam to meet the other two teams in Ramayapatnam on Tuesday the November 3rd.

 

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay has expressed grief over the death of fishermen and announced a solatium of 7 lakh rupees for the family of the deceased. Out of which 2 lakh rupees would be released immediately. He has also ordered that the bodies of the deceased be brought back to Tamil Nadu at state expense to be handed over to their families.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has called on Commonwealth countries to de-risk and diversify their supply chains, emphasising the need for shorter, trusted routes, improved connectivity and stronger local distribution networks to promote trade and economic cooperation. He said member countries needed to make greater efforts to strengthen their economic partnerships and build resilient supply chains.

 

Dr Jaishankar was addressing the Commonwealth Heads of Government and Business Leaders Breakfast Meeting on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2026 in St. John’s, Antigua and Barbuda.

 

He said, more connectivity corridors are good for business. Commonwealth partners should make more efforts to enhance local distribution.

 

Dr Jaishankar also called for greater focus on vocational training and capacity building, saying these would provide member countries with more options. He described the Indian business community spread across the world as an important asset for the Commonwealth.

The government has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in the country, including certain Pakistani citizens, minority refugees, registered Sri Lankan Tamils and Tibetans. The Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) Order, 2026, was published in the Official Gazette by the Home Ministry. It introduced a definition of the Visa Manual issued by the Central Government from time to time, which incorporates instructions relating to visas, immigration, and other connected matters. Under the revised provisions, Indian citizens travelling to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air will be exempted from passport requirement, subject to producing any one of the identity documents specified in the Visa Manual before an Immigration Officer. They will also be required to provide any information sought by the officer. Similar provisions apply to citizens of Nepal and Bhutan entering or exiting India.

 Dhanteras is being celebrated today. The festival, which falls just before Diwali, is considered a symbol of wealth, good health, and prosperity. On Dhanteras, devotees worship Lord Dhanvantari, Goddess Lakshmi, and Lord Kuber. According to popular belief, performing puja and making purchases during the auspicious hours on this day brings happiness, wealth, and prosperity to the household. People mostly buying gold, silver, utensils, vehicles, and other new items is a long-standing tradition on Dhanteras.

 

<><><> 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people on the occasion of Dhanteras today. In a social media post, Mr Modi expressed hope that the divine grace of Lord Dhanvantari illuminate everyone’s life with happiness, peace, and excellent health. He wished that an eternal flame of joy and enthusiasm continues to shine in every household.

Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi who played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

 A fire broke out at Puri Plaza at Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh. According to Delhi Fire Services, a call was received at 1:30 am, after which 27 fire tenders were deployed to contain the fire. No casualties have been reported so far, and firefighting operations are underway. Further details are awaited.

Israel’s Arab parties have agreed to support Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot as Prime Minister. Eisenkot has secured the backing of 67 out of 120 Knesset members following historic endorsements from Israel’s major Arab-led political factions, placing him ahead of incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

 

According to The Times of Israel and The Jerusalem Post, the agreement was reached yesterday during official post-election consultations with President Isaac Herzog. The support puts Eisenkot ahead of Prime Minister Netanyahu, whose bloc has 53 seats. President Isaac Herzog has begun consultations with political parties following last week’s election and will appoint the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. The chosen candidate will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to form a coalition and failure could trigger another election.

Defending champion India beat Japan 4-1 in the finals of Asian Hockey Championship in Mohali to lift the title for the record sixth time. More from our correspondent:

 

“Although this was India’s third successive title but the winning team has to earn it against a strong defense by the rival team. An early lead by the Samurais kept Indian Tigers on the toes till the end of the 3rd quarter when it equalized the goal. The fourth and last quarter was dominated by India as the boys striked thrice to take an unassailable lead and won the Gold. India’s title-winning run was a perfect farewell to midfielder Nilakanta Sharma, who played his last international match in the national jersey. In another match for Bronze, Malaysia defeated South Korea by 5-2 . Rajesh Bali, Akashvani News, Jalandhar.”

 

Celebrating India’s title win, Hockey India has announced a cash reward of 3 lakh rupees for each player and 1.5 lakh rupees for each member of the support staff.

India’s Tanvi Patri created history at the 2026 Summer Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, by becoming the first Indian woman to win a silver medal in badminton singles. She lost a thrilling final to reigning World Junior Champion Zhang Yi Xin of China, despite saving six match points. Tanvi became the first Indian female shuttler to reach the Youth Olympics badminton final. Before her, HS Prannoy and Lakshya Sen had won individual silver medals at the Games.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala and Mahe today. According to IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Odisha today. The Met Department has predicted similar weather conditions over Coastal and South Interior Karnataka and Lakshadweep for today.

In a major overhaul of Agnipath scheme, the Union Cabinet has approved a revised framework creating a pathway for 100 percent absorption of all willing Agniveers into the Defence Forces. Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani said, the move follows an extensive evaluation by the armed forces that gave highly positive feedback on Agniveer efficacy, physical fitness, and technological adaptability.

 

The decision comes just before the first batch of 18,300 Agniveers completes its initial four-year tenure next month.

 

“As originally planned, the top 25% of Agniveers will be offered regular permanent employment immediately after their initial 4-year tenure based on merit. The remaining 75% of Agniveers will now be given an additional engagement period of two years, subject to candidate willingness and recommendations from the forces.

 

Upon finishing the additional two-year extension (bringing total service to 6 years), all remaining willing Agniveers will be offered permanent enrolment as regular soldiers, provided they meet standard selection criteria.

The newly added two-year extension period will feature increased monthly remuneration, an enhanced Seva Nidhi package, and cumulative seniority benefits.

 

The structural reforms effectively remove the mandatory 75% exit provision, ensuring that any Agniveer who wishes to serve permanently and meets the benchmark criteria will have a direct route to do so. YASHASVI KIRYAL, for Akashvani News, DELHI.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will interact with members of the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Para Games 2026, at the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex in New Delhi today.  He will also address the gathering on the occasion.

India recorded its best-ever performance at the Asian Para Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with 97 para-athletes winning a total of 114 medals. The medal tally includes 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals. The programme will be attended by the medal-winning athletes, coaches, officials of the Paralympic Committee of India and the Indian Olympic Association, representatives of National Sports Federations, and officials of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has launched the ‘Khelo Bharat: From Manufacturing to Podium Finish Quiz’ on the MY Bharat portal. The quiz aims to raise awareness about the government’s efforts to strengthen country’s sports ecosystem. It also promotes domestic sports goods manufacturing and innovation. The Ministry said the initiative highlights country’s participation and achievements at the 20th Asian Games 2026 and 5th Asian Para Games 2026, held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The quiz is open to citizens, students, youth, professionals and sports enthusiasts. It will remain open until 20th of this month.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah will inaugurate a martyrs’ memorial in Ambala Cantt today, built in memory of the brave martyrs of the first war of independence in 1857. BJP leader and former minister Aseem Goel shared this information during a press conference in Ambala yesterday. He stated that this is not merely the inauguration of a memorial, but a historic occasion to express the nation’s gratitude. Mr. Goel mentioned that this grand memorial, constructed over an area of approximately 22 acres at a cost of around Rs 800 crore, will establish a distinct identity as a part of Haryana’s historical heritage. The names of over 700 brave martyrs associated with the 1857 freedom struggle have been inscribed in golden letters at the memorial. He further stated that following the inauguration of the martyrs’ memorial, the Union Home Minister will address a large public meeting at Gandhi Ground in Ambala.

Prior to this, Mr. Amit Shah will lead a padyatra (foot march) in Karnal organized as part of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao campaign from Sector 12 to Mughal Canal of the city.

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, to provide for immediate suspension of manufacturing licences in respect of drugs declared Not of Standard Quality on specified critical quality parameters. The proposed amendments seek to enable prompt regulatory intervention upon detection of substandard medicines, prevent their continued manufacture and distribution, and strengthen the mechanism for ensuring compliance in the interest of patient safety and public health.

 

“The Health Ministry said that under the existing provisions, suspension or cancellation of a manufacturing licence is preceded by the prescribed regulatory procedure, including issuance of a show-cause notice. The Ministry added that the proposed amendment also provides for mandatory corrective measures before revocation of the suspension. The suspension shall continue until the manufacturer undertakes an effective Root Cause Analysis and implements appropriate Corrective and Preventive Action to the satisfaction of the concerned Licensing Authority. The Ministry said that the amendments are expected to strengthen post-marketing regulatory surveillance, facilitate timely action against substandard medicines, promote greater accountability among manufacturers and marketers. The draft amendments have been notified for public consultation and  objections and suggestions have been invited  from stakeholders and members of the public within 30 days. With ANAND KUMAR, SHIVANG MISRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

The Uttar Pradesh Board of Secondary Education has decided to introduce a new format of answer sheets for the 2027 High School and Intermediate examinations. The move aims to make the examination system more secure, transparent and free from malpractices.

 

“Under the new arrangement, answer sheets will have a single main cover carrying a QR code. On scanning the code, the logo of the Uttar Pradesh Board of Secondary Education will appear. The Board has also decided to use different colours for answer sheets of Class 10 and Class 12. For High School, the A copies will be dark orange and B copies dark blue. For Intermediate, the A copies will be purple and B copies green. The Board has also made special arrangements for the security of answer sheets. They will be kept in secure rooms under round-the-clock CCTV surveillance. Serial numbers of answer sheet bundles will also be recorded in registers to ensure proper monitoring of their storage and distribution. The High School and Intermediate examinations will be held from the 5th to the 24th of February, 2027. Om Awasthi, akashvani news, Lucknow.“

The  Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has cautioned  banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and fintech firms about a growing trend of financially motivated cyberattacks involving artificial intelligence agents. In an advisory issued to financial institutions, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre , which functions under the Union Home Ministry has asked financial institutions to urgently implement measures prescribed  in  the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team advisories.

US President Donald Trump acknowledged that the eight-month-old war in Iran heavily impacted the midterm elections. Speaking to reporters at the White House after the midterm election results, Trump conceded that voters were deeply frustrated by the surging gas prices tied to the conflict.

 

“Democrats swept the polls taking control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Despite the severe political fallout for the Republican Party, Trump firmly defended his foreign policy agenda, asserting that the military campaign was an absolute necessity.  Trump emphasized that preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon remains his long-term priority. He also rejected the notion that the blowout election results were a personal rebuke, noting that he himself was not on the ballot.

US Vice President JD Vance distanced himself from the administration’s military strategy, and said that “the reason we lost is the war”. Meanwhile, Mike Johnson of Louisiana announced he will not seek reelection as House Republican leader, setting up an intense intra-party leadership battle.

 

Following the news of the Democratic sweep, global energy markets responded immediately. Brent crude oil futures plunged over 8% down to under 100 dollars a barrel for the first time in nearly a month.

 

Incoming Democratic congressional leaders have pledged a swift legislative agenda focused on lo  wering the domestic cost of gas, groceries, and healthcare, alongside launching sweeping oversight investigations into the Trump administration’s conduct of the war. Jigyasa Pandey for Akashvani News.”

Bahamas has joined as the 116th member of the International Solar Alliance (ISA). Bahamas’ High Commissioner Peter Nicholas Symonette Jr. handed over the Instrument of Accession to the ISA Framework Agreement to Joint Secretary, Economic Diplomacy and Head of Depository, PS Gangadhar. This was done on the sidelines of the Ninth Session of the ISA Assembly in New Delhi.

In hockey, India will take on Japan in final of Asian Champions Trophy in Mohali today. The match will start at 7 PM at Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium. Defending champions India secured their place in the final with an authoritative 8-1 victory over South Korea in the semi-finals yesterday. Japan earned their spot in the final through a hard-fought battle against Malaysia. Malaysia will face South Korea for Bronze medal match.

 

“The jubilation was all around as India dominantly entered the finals by thumping the sporting rivals Korea. Those who were cheering the team included 1975 World Cup Hockey winning Captain Ajitpal Singh and Aslam Sher Khan besides Zafar Iqbal, Olympian Balbir Singh Randhawa and Rajinder Singh Senior. Dashing Shilanand Lakra and Dilpreet Singh both hit the goal post twice besides Captain Harmanpreet Singh and other teamates who contributed with a single goal each. Sangjun Han from Korea was the face saver with the single goal. Earlier, China bruised Bangladesh 3-1 to be placed on 5th position in the tournament. It is yet to be seen that how the defending champions and five-time winner of the Asian Champions Trophy – India, will dribble the Samurais in the final. Rajesh Bali for Akashvani News.”

Vote counting is underway across the United States following the 2026 midterm elections, with Democrats taking an early lead over President Donald Trump’s Republicans as results continue to come in.

         

 

 

Democrats have secured ten Senate victories, two House win and six gubernatorial victories, while Republicans have won three Senate seat and one gubernatorial victories, when report last come in.

         

 

 

In the US Senate races, Democratic incumbent Mark Warner secured a fourth term representing Virginia, defeating Republican Bert Mizusawa. In Georgia, Democrat Jon Ossoff won re-election to the Senate, defeating Republican Mike Collins.

         

 

 

In Delaware, Democratic incumbent Chris Coons defeated Republican Mike Katz to secure a third full Senate term, while Rhode Island Senator Jack Reed won a sixth term after defeating Republican Raymond McKay.

 

 

 

In New Jersey, Democratic Senator Cory Booker also retained his seat, defeating Republican challenger Justin Murphy.

         

 

 

In Florida, Republican Ashley Moody won the US Senate race, defeating Democrat Angie Nixon.

         

 

 

In the gubernatorial contests, Democrats JB Pritzker of Illinois, Kathy Hochul of New York, Phil Weiser of Colorado, Helena Foulkes of Rhode Island, Josh Shapiro of Pennsylvania and Wes Moore of Maryland won the election. Republican Eric Barlow won the Wyoming gubernatorial race, defeating Democrat Kenneth Casner.

         

 

 

Meanwhile, in the US House races, Democrats Debbie Wasserman Schultz of Florida and Jamie Ager of North Carolina secured victories, defeating their Republican challengers.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that India aims to achieve defence production worth 3 lakh crore rupees and defence exports of 50 thousand crore rupees by 2029. Addressing the Consultative Committee of Defence Ministry of Defence in Jaisalmer, Mr Singh said the government is committed to building a technologically empowered military capable of meeting present-day and emerging security challenges. He said defence production had increased from 46 thousand 429 crore rupees in 2014-15 to a record 1.78 lakh crore rupees in 2025-26.Defence exports has risen from less than 2,000 crore rupees in 2014 to approximately 40,000 crore rupees.

Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) has successfully test-fired an indigenous Pralay quasi-ballistic missile from the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur, off the Odisha coast. The missile was launched from Launch Complex-Three yesterday. It successfully engaged two simulated targets at a reported distance of around 500 kilometers. As a safety precaution, authorities evacuated more than 2,500 people from nearby villages before the test. The Pralay missile is capable of carrying different types of warheads and has a reported strike range of up to 500 kilometers.

Government has launched the indigenous, AI Foundational Models Eka- 1 by Soket Labs and Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B by ZenteiQ. Speaking on the occasion, Secretary of Electronics and IT Ministry S Krishnan said, the public release of these foundational AI models marks an important step towards building a strong and strategic AI ecosystem in the country. He said that these models have several potential applications including cyber security and can significantly enhance productivity and operational efficiency.  Emphasising their importance, Mr Krishnan noted that these models can also be deployed in air-gapped environments, opening new possibilities for secure and enterprise – based Artificial intelligence applications in the country.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said the Central Reserve Police Force-CRPF completed 12 consecutive months without any operational casualty for the first time in 47 years. In a social media post, Mr Modi said, a zero that speaks volumes. The paramilitary force has not suffered a single operational fatality anywhere in the country over a year.

         

 

 

In a social media post, CRPF Director General Gyanendra Pratap Singh shared data on operational fatalities in the force over the last fifty years, noting that the last fatality was on 30th October, last year. He said, improved hardware, better training, strategic planning and deployment and quick injured evacuation to secondary and tertiary medical care facilities have contributed to this.

The Andhra Pradesh Government has intensified rescue, relief and precautionary measures in view of heavy rainfall and flooding caused by Cyclone Murasu. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed district authorities to remain on high alert and ensure the safety of people in vulnerable and low-lying areas. More than twelve thousand people have been shifted to safer locations, while National and State Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed in the affected districts. A report:

 

 

 

         

 

 

“The Chief Minister reviewed the situation through a teleconference with collectors of twelve districts and directed them to closely monitor rainfall, floodwater movement and relief operations. Bapatla , Naguluppalapadu recorded twenty centimetres of rainfall each, while Yadlapadu in Palnadu district received twenty-five centimetres. Heavy rainfall was also reported in Prakasam, Guntur ,NTR and other coastal districts.

         

 

 

The administration has established 480 relief centres and deployed 11 State Disaster Response Force and 13 National Disaster Response Force teams. In Bapatla district, 2,650 people were evacuated to 67 relief centres, while police personnel and emergency response teams cleared 333 fallen trees to restore road connectivity. Five fishermen from Oduru village in Bapatla district, who went missing at sea, were rescued safely by officials near Muthukur in Nellore district. Ministers and district officials have been instructed to coordinate across departments, monitor reservoirs and flood channels. Ravala Sai Gireesh, for Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

The National Conference of Chairpersons of Public Accounts Committees will conclude in Thiruvananthapuram today. More  from our correspondent:

         

 

 

“The conference brings together Chairpersons of the Public Accounts Committees of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of various States and Union Territories.

The conference, inaugurated yesterday by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, focused on ensuring legislative oversight over public expenditure and strengthening the role of Public Accounts Committees.

The plenary sessions will continue this morning. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla will deliver the valedictory address at 11.45 a.m. Smithy M Palluruthy, Akashvani News, Thiruvananthapuram.”

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will launch the ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’  in New Delhi today to strengthen intergenerational solidarity and promote a society that values the experience, wisdom and contribution of senior citizens. The campaign will be formally launched by the Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Virendra Kumar. It seeks to institutionalise meaningful and sustained engagement between senior citizens and younger generations. The campaign will also try to infuse mutual respect, understanding, and companionship and shared responsibility among the young generation for the senior citizens.

An Indian national was killed and 3 others injured when 2 helicopters collided while attempting to land at Pheriche helipad in Nepal’s Solukhumbu district yesterday. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

         

 

 

“According to Nepal’s Civil Aviation Authority, one helicopter operated by Air Dynasty had flown from Lukla, while the Fishtail Air helicopter was carrying 2 foreign passengers from Gorakshep.

The deceased has been identified as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu from Tamil Nadu. Fishtail Air said his mortal remains were brought to Kathmandu for post-mortem examination. The other passenger and its captain are stable and out of danger.

The aviation authority has launched an investigation into the accident and said further action will be taken based on its findings. ARVIND KUMAR JAIN,AKASHVANI NEWS,KATHMANDU.”

In hockey, the unbeaten India will take on South Korea in the semi-final of the 9th Hero Asian Hockey Championship at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali, today. In the league stage matches played at Jalandhar, India remained on the top by winning all 5 matches, followed by Japan at the second position, Malaysia third, South Korea fourth, China fifth and Bangladesh at the last pedestal. More from our correspondent:

The government has notified a new set of rules governing India’s civil aviation sector, replacing the nearly nine-decade-old Aircraft Rules, 1937. The new rules called the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, will come into effect on 1st of January, next year. The rules provide the regulatory framework on various aspects of the aviation sector including aircraft registration, manufacturing, safety certification, maintenance, flight operations, personnel licensing and airport operations.

 

Airlines operating scheduled air services are required to determine fares based on factors such as operating costs and submit tariff details to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA). The provision allows the Centre to issue written directions if it determines that an extraordinary situation has arisen and intervention is necessary in the public interest. The new rules also mandate greater transparency in airfare pricing, requiring airlines to publish their fares on official websites and other digital platforms. The DGCA will continue to monitor tariffs set by scheduled airlines. One of the key areas covered by the rules is the registration and certification of aircraft. They specify requirements for registering aircraft in India and obtaining certificates that establish whether an aircraft is safe to fly.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has reviewed preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in 18 districts across four divisions and directed senior officials to strengthen voter lists, security arrangements and personnel training to ensure free, fair and peaceful polling.

The review meeting was chaired by Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg in Meerut in the presence of Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa and other senior commission officials, according to a statement issued by the CEO’s office.

 

Mr Garg emphasised the importance of the review for both first-time district election officers and police chiefs and experienced officials, noting that election rules and guidelines undergo periodic changes. He urged all officials to examine the issues discussed afresh and improve their preparations accordingly.

 

He also stressed ensuring minimum assured facilities at polling stations and launching EVM awareness programmes. The senior deputy election commissioner instructed authorities to maintain strict surveillance against the illegal transportation and distribution of liquor during the elections, including checks at distilleries’ source and exit points.

 

He also called for effective arrangements for mobile phone deposit boxes at polling stations on polling day, with the assistance of volunteers. Officials were asked to ensure training for state-level master trainers and familiarise relevant personnel with postal ballot-related instructions.

 

Rinwa directed officials to launch special drives in classes 11 and 12 and degree colleges to enrol young people becoming eligible to vote for the first time. He also asked authorities to re-examine rejected Form 6 applications to ensure that eligible citizens are included in electoral rolls.

 

Applicants filling Form 6 should provide their mobile numbers and complete addresses accurately, while Common Service Centre operators should be trained immediately in the online application process and measures to prevent multiple entries. The CEO further directed district election officers to recheck all Forms 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since the conclusion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The CEO also directed officials to ensure distribution of voter information slips five days before polling and record the distribution in booth-level officers’ registers.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved Northern Bullet Train Corridor which will connect Delhi to Guwahati via Siliguri. This was disclosed by Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw in Varanasi yesterday. The Minister was in the city to flag off Varanasi-New Delhi Vande Bharat Sleeper Express. Several important financial, tax, and administrative changes have come into effect from today. Small businesses selling goods online will find it easier to register across states, while taxpayers can expect faster refunds. The changes were approved at the 57th GST Council meeting last month. Small suppliers operating through e-commerce platforms will no longer need to maintain a physical office in every state where their goods are stored, provided they meet the prescribed conditions. A REPORT…..

 

“Sellers passing on input tax credit of up to 2.5 rupees lakh a month will be allowed to declare an e-commerce platform’s warehouse as their principal place of business in states where they have no physical presence. The reforms also introduce automated processing for certain categories of GST refunds. Claims for the entire excess balance in a taxpayer’s electronic cash ledger will be sanctioned automatically, without requiring intervention from a tax officer. For refunds relating to zero-rated supplies and inverted duty structures, 90 per cent of the claimed amount will be provisionally sanctioned through an automated, risk-based system. All asset management companies will be required to make direct plans the default option on their digital investment platforms from today. Pensioners below 80 years of age can submit their annual life certificates from today till 30th of this month. The Department of Telecommunications has made it mandatory for telecom service providers to implement Calling Name Presentation services from today. The feature will display the caller’s name along with the phone number on incoming calls, making it easier for users to identify callers and helping curb anonymous and potentially fraudulent calls. ANUPAM MISHRA, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

A Winter Action Plan will come into effect in the national capital from today to combat air pollution. The Delhi Government has said that under the plan, vehicles from outside Delhi that do not comply with BS-VI emission standards will not be allowed to enter the national capital. The city government will also impose restrictions on construction and demolition activities to curb dust pollution. Construction sites will be monitored through AI-enabled cameras directly connected to the government’s Command and Control Centre. The Winter Action Plan also includes the implementation of 50 per cent work-from-home and the ‘No PUC, No Fuel’ policy. Under this policy, vehicle owners will not be able to purchase petrol, diesel, CNG or LPG at fuel stations unless their vehicles have a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate

The government has constituted a High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat to review the country’s banking sector and recommend reforms in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The Finance Ministry said, the Committee will recommend structural, institutional, regulatory and legislative reforms to make the Indian banking sector globally competitive, financially inclusive and resilient. The Committee will be chaired by former Central Vigilance Commissioner Suresh N. Patel.

“The High level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat  will have a tenure of six months. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced the setting up of the Committee in her Budget speech this year. The Committee will assess existing banking practices and prudential norms, identify global best practices and examine their suitability for adoption in the Indian banking system. It will also review the existing regulatory and legal frameworks governing banks, including Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks, and suggest reforms to improve efficiency and ease of banking. In addition, the Committee will prepare a roadmap for the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital innovations in banking institutions, while recommending safeguards against cyber risks. With Rishu Jaiswal, Shivang Misra, Akashavni News, Delhi.”

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has successfully launched its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-03, marking a significant step towards strengthening the country’s indigenous satellite navigation capabilities. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, GSLV-F18, carrying the satellite, lifted off from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, last night.  NVS-03 is the third satellite in ISRO’s second-generation navigation satellite series. It is designed to ensure continuity and improve the availability of navigation services under the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), country’s indigenous alternative to the Global Positioning System (GPS).  Speaking to media later, Dr Narayanan said ISRO has placed its third indigenous atomic clock in orbit aboard the NVS-03 navigation satellite.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated the scientists, engineers and the entire team of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 rocket carrying the NVS-03 satellite.
